scenes.headline: How one policy steers a humanoid robot
scenes.sub: Metatron v1 for the Unitree G1
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Servo! This is one network that walks, interacts and recovers for a humanoid robot. Let's see what goes in and what comes out.

scenes.text: One transformer reads the robot's own state plus optional goals, and writes a joint target for all 29 joints.
scenes.say: One transformer reads the robot's own state and any goals you switch on. Then it writes a target for every joint.

steps.say: The robot's own state is small. Its history of eight steps is bigger.
Goals are the largest input, but a mask decides whether they count at all.
A six layer transformer reads everything at once.
Its raw action becomes a joint target by a fixed offset and scale.

parts.note: a quarter of the effort limit over stiffness

scenes.say: The target is the standing pose plus a scale times the raw output. The scale is a quarter of the effort limit divided by stiffness.

scenes.label: per step on a shared CPU, against a 20 ms budget
scenes.say: On a shared processor one step takes fifty three to seventy eight milliseconds. Fifty hertz needs twenty.

scenes.label: change in the action from a masked-off goal
scenes.note: the same noise moved it by up to 0.76 once the mask was on
scenes.say: Noise in a masked off goal changed the action by exactly zero. Switch the mask on, and it matters.

scenes.text: Test the policy as a function first: the same state gives the same action, and masks decide which inputs count.
scenes.say: The same state gives the same action, and masks decide which inputs count. Test it as a function before you test it on a robot.

recap: Not yet checked in a closed loop
scenes.say: One transformer, many inputs, exact masks. Whether it keeps the robot upright is a question for a simulator.
